Subject: Retention mechanics for EU pilot: what we keep, purge triggers, and SLA exception request

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for kicking off the EU pilot with us. A few quick asks from BrightBank came up during the runbook review and I want to confirm Redwood's practical retention mechanics so we can map them to your regulatory obligations. High level questions below — please reply with anything that needs correcting on our side.

1) What is captured by default for hosted API calls in the EU region? Specifically: request metadata, full prompt text, model outputs, and any derived artifacts (summaries, embeddings).
2) What triggers deletions? Is it time-based TTL only, or do manual purges / customer-initiated deletions remove copies from all backup tiers?
3) Can we provide audit logs showing when/where a given request was retained and purged (time, cluster id, retention-policy-id)?
4) BrightBank has a regulatory ask: retain full request/response payloads for 180 days for a scoped pilot. Can Redwood accept an SLA exception and where does that sit commercially/technically?

I've attached the BrightBank_Security_QA.xlsx with the list of endpoints and sample PII contexts. The pilot start date is 2027-05-20 so it'd be great to resolve this this week.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alice —

Looping in Karthik (product infra) and Kimberly (legal). Below are working definitions we use internally; Karthik please correct anything imprecise and add technical notes about EU residency.

- Prompt: the user-supplied text/context included in a request (including system and assistant messages for chat).
- Generated output: the model-produced tokens returned to the caller as the API response.
- Derived artifact: any artifact produced by downstream processing such as embeddings, reranking scores, or automated summaries created by Redwood services.

High-level default policy (hosted, EU region):
- Minimal telemetry (request timestamp, route, model, token counts, latency) retained by default for 30 days for debugging and billing.
- Full payload capture (prompt + generated output) is NOT stored by default in hosted plan unless the customer opts in via a data-capture flag or purchases the "debug-retain" add-on.
- When full payloads are stored (opt-in), they are stored for a customer-configurable TTL — default 30 days, configurable up to 180 days for enterprise contracts.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, summaries) follow the same capture setting as payloads; if payloads are not stored, derived artifacts are not persisted unless explicitly enabled.

Karthik / Kimberly — can you confirm the above and outline how we would operationalize an EU 180-day exception for BrightBank (technical steps, approvals, timeline)?

Thanks,
Grace
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alice Jansen <alice.jansen@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Retention mechanics for EU pilot: what we keep, purge triggers, and SLA exception request

Thanks Grace — adding the technical detail Alice asked for and clarifying residency/purge behavior.

1) Definitions (formal):
- prompt: unredacted request.payload.input_text + system_metadata (if present).
- generated output: response.payload.tokens as returned via the API.
- derived artifact: any persisted object produced by Redwood pipelines (embeddings, reranker indexes, persistent caches).

2) Default capture mechanics (EU-hosted):
- Telemetry (route/model/latency/token-count/event-metrics): stored in metrics store for 30 days, aggregated thereafter. No payload contents.
- Full payloads: only stored when customer enables the "store_full_payloads" setting on their account or when the customer uses Redwood Dedicated where admins can enable persistent payload stores.
- When enabled, payloads are stored in the EU data plane in a segregated bucket with a per-account TTL.

3) Deletion / purge semantics:
- Time-based TTL: objects are assigned a retention TTL on write; background worker enforces deletion once TTL expires.
- Manual purge: customers may request an immediate purge via the Console or API. Manual purge enqueues deletion jobs that remove objects from primary storage and mark tombstones; full removal from backups can take up to 72 hours because of snapshot lifecycle.
- Legal/forensic holds: If BrightBank requests a legal hold, we can exempt certain records from TTL-based deletion until released, subject to documented approval.

4) Audit logs and chain of custody:
- We can produce an export that shows: request_id, timestamp, cluster_id, retention_policy_id, store_flag (true/false), storage_bucket_id, and deletion_timestamp (when applicable).
- Sample audit export can be produced redacted for PII for your auditors.

5) How to enable 180-day retention for the pilot (summary):
- Commercial: sign an SLA amendment (we have a standard exception template).
- Technical: we enable "store_full_payloads" for the scoped pilot account in the EU data plane and set TTL to 180 days.
- Ops: schedule a maintenance window to ensure the account is placed into the dedicated retention tier; estimated lead time 7-10 business days after signed amendment.

I'll drop a sample audit log CSV and the standard SLA exception template for legal to review. Marissa, please coordinate the operational ticket with onboarding.

- Karthik

Hi Alice —

Legal has reviewed the request and the draft SLA exception. We can accommodate a scoped 180-day retention for BrightBank's pilot under the following conditions:

1) Signed SLA amendment (attached).
2) BrightBank agrees to a scoped account definition (list of endpoints and internal teams) — no broader cross-account capture.
3) Redwood will execute manual purge guarantees as follows: primary store deletion within 24 hours of request; backup/snapshot removal completed within 72 hours of purge job completion.

Next steps:
- I've attached the SLA_exception_form.pdf (editable). Please confirm signatories and we will initiate the DocuSign envelope.
- Product & Ops (Karthik / Marissa) will open the infra ticket to enable store_full_payloads for the pilot account upon receipt of the signed amendment. Estimated activation window 7-10 business days.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
